question: Among more than 40,000 Japanese adults followed for seven years, what happened to those who reported no ikigai?
answer: They died at about one and a half times the rate. In the Ohsaki cohort of adults aged 40 to 79, those who said they had no ikigai, a sense of life worth living, had higher mortality over seven years. Reports of purpose and health may partly feed each other.
move: Name one thing you would be sorry to lose, and tend it.
reference: Sone and colleagues, Sense of life worth living (ikigai) and mortality in Japan: Ohsaki Study, Psychosomatic Medicine, 2008
